questions.question: In Livy's story, why did the ruined former soldier first borrow money?
options: To pay a tax
To pay his daughter's dowry
To buy new weapons
To buy seed for planting
To pay a ransom to raiders
questions.explanation: He borrowed to pay a tax, and crushing interest swallowed his grandfather's farm and then his father's. Finally his creditors imprisoned and whipped him.
questions.sourceQuote: Back home, he borrowed to pay a tax, and crushing interest swallowed his grandfather's farm, then his father's.

questions.question: What was the plebeians' main price for returning to Rome after the first secession?
options: A complete written code of Roman law
A share of the land conquered from the Sabines
Permanent seats for plebeians in the Senate
A new official chosen from the plebs to protect them
The right to elect one of the two consuls
questions.explanation: The plebs demanded an official chosen from among themselves to shield them from the consuls. The Senate agreed, creating the tribune of the plebs.
questions.sourceQuote: Their price for returning was a new kind of official, chosen from among the plebs, to protect them from the power of the consuls.

questions.question: Which Twelve Tables rule worked against the plebeians?
options: A ban on plebeians speaking in court
A ban on plebeians entering temples
A ban on plebeians serving in the army
A ban on plebeians owning farmland
A ban on marriage between patricians and plebeians
questions.explanation: One law banned marriage between patricians and plebeians. The Tables' debt rules were also harsh, though at least clear.
questions.sourceQuote: Not everything helped the plebs: one law banned marriage between patricians and plebeians.

questions.question: What puzzle in the official lists of consuls troubles historians?
options: They show no consuls at all before 400 BC
They name several consuls known to be Greek
They include plebeian family names in the fifth century BC
They leave out every year of the decemvirs
Some years list three consuls instead of two
questions.explanation: Men with plebeian family names appear as consuls in the fifth century BC. Yet the post was supposedly closed to plebeians then.
questions.sourceQuote: Official lists of consuls include men with plebeian family names in the fifth century BC, when the post was supposedly closed to them.

questions.question: Under the Twelve Tables, who owned fruit that fell from a tree onto a neighbour's land?
options: The Roman state
Whoever picked it up first
Both owners shared it equally
The neighbour
The owner of the tree
questions.explanation: Fallen fruit still belonged to the tree's owner. Such specific everyday rules are typical of the Twelve Tables.
questions.sourceQuote: Fruit falling onto a neighbour's land still belonged to the tree's owner.

questions.question: What did the Lex Publilia of 471 BC change?
options: Debt slavery would be abolished
Plebeians would vote by tribe rather than by curia
One consul each year had to be a plebeian
Plebiscites would now bind all Romans
Tribunes would become members of the Senate
questions.explanation: Plebeians would now vote by tribe, districts of citizens, and elect tribunes this way. This freed them from the influence of patrician patrons.
questions.sourceQuote: Plebeians would now gather and vote by tribe, districts of citizens, rather than by curia, and tribunes would be elected this way.

questions.question: Which peoples was Rome at war with in 494 BC, when the plebeian soldiers refused to march? (select all that apply)
options: The Samnites
The Aequi
The Sabines
The Volsci
The Etruscans
questions.explanation: Rome faced the Sabines, Aequi and Volsci in 494 BC. The Aequi and Volsci were hill tribes to the east and south-east.
questions.sourceQuote: In 494 BC Rome was at war with three neighbouring peoples: the Sabines, and the Aequi and Volsci, hill tribes to the east and south-east.

questions.question: How far did a tribune's protection extend?
options: Within Rome and a mile beyond
Throughout the whole of Italy
Only inside the Forum itself
Wherever the Roman army marched
Within ten miles of the city
questions.explanation: A tribune's protection held only within Rome and a mile beyond. He also had to be physically present to intervene.
questions.sourceQuote: A tribune had to be physically present to intervene, and his protection held only within Rome and a mile beyond.

questions.question: Why did the Senate raise the number of tribunes to ten in 457 BC?
options: To defuse the campaign for written law
To replace the consuls during a plague
To reward the plebs for a victory in war
To give one tribune to each new tribe
To welcome envoys returning from Greece
questions.explanation: The Senate hoped extra tribunes would calm the push for written law. It had already stalled for five years, citing war and plague.
questions.sourceQuote: In 457 BC the Senate tried to defuse the campaign by raising the number of tribunes to ten.

questions.question: What did the second board of decemvirs do when their term ended?
options: Refused to step down and ruled without tribunes
Asked the plebs to extend their term
Published the final laws and retired
Fled Rome to escape prosecution
Handed power to two newly elected consuls
questions.explanation: The decemvirs clung to power, with no tribunes to check them and no right of appeal. They even had a former tribune who criticised them killed.
questions.sourceQuote: When their term ended they refused to step down, ruling with no tribunes to check them and no right of appeal.
